overview: Spicy's Spider turns any wall into a ladder. Its only active code is an EventOnLadder post handler: when the player is collided horizontally and the mode setting is 'Vanilla' — the only mode in the ModeSetting — it sets the event's onLadder flag true. The event is dispatched from the fork's EntityLivingBase.isOnLadder(), which computes the vanilla ladder state (the block under the player is ladder or vine, and the player is not a spectator), fires the POST event, and returns the module-modified value whenever it differs from the block check. The client's movement code then applies vanilla ladder physics — horizontal motion clamped to ±0.15, fall distance zeroed, and, while collided horizontally, a 0.2 upward motion per tick — so the player climbs any wall at 0.2 blocks per tick with no ladder present. The wire effect is a C03 stream showing a sustained +0.2 vertical distance next to non-climbable blocks.

sections.p: EntityLivingBase.isOnLadder() (line 1132) reads the block at the player's feet, computes the vanilla ladder boolean, constructs an EventOnLadder, dispatches it with EventType.POST, and returns e.onLadder when the modules changed it. Spider's handler sets onLadder = true exactly when isCollidedHorizontally, so the client believes it is on a climbable while touching any solid wall. The ModeSetting wraps a single option, 'Vanilla', so the mode switch is vestigial — there is no other mode to select.

The ladder motion lives in EntityLivingBase.onLivingUpdate (line 1645): while isOnLadder() is true, motionX and motionZ are clamped to ±0.15, fallDistance resets to zero, and the collided-horizontally branch (line 1667) sets motionY = 0.2. Because isOnLadder() now reports true against plain walls, the player ascends at a constant 0.2 blocks per tick while touching the wall — a vertical profile with no vanilla counterpart, since vanilla only ascends via the jump impulse. Each tick the C03 stream reports that +0.2 y-distance, which is the entire server-visible surface.

files.label: Spider.java (module)
files.explanation:
The module is two small handlers. The EventUpdate pre branch only writes the current mode into additionalInformation. The EventOnLadder post branch is the exploit: if isCollidedHorizontally and the mode is 'Vanilla', it sets the event's onLadder field true — a single boolean write that the fork's isOnLadder() dispatcher honors.

resetSettings and addSettings show the configuration surface: one ModeSetting with one mode. The Module base class handles the toggle lifecycle; there is no onEnable or onDisable logic, so the module's entire behavior is the flag write.

files.label: EntityLivingBase.java (ladder dispatch and consumption)
files.explanation:
Two regions of this file make the module work. isOnLadder() (line 1132) is the hook point: it computes the vanilla ladder boolean from the block under the player, dispatches EventOnLadder POST, and substitutes the event's onLadder value when modules changed it — the exact contract Spider exploits. onLivingUpdate (line 1645) is the consumer: while isOnLadder() is true it clamps horizontal motion to ±0.15, clears fallDistance, and, under the isCollidedHorizontally branch (line 1667), drives motionY to 0.2.

Because the substitution happens before the movement code reads the ladder state, the module never has to touch motion or packets: the vanilla climb code does all the work once the boolean lies.

countering.label: SurvivalFly (vertical envelope and climbable exemption)
countering.explanation:
SurvivalFly rebuilds the allowed vertical from the physics model via vDistRel. The jump envelope (PhysicsEnvelope.isJumpMotion) admits only the initial jump impulse; after that the allowance is momentum-seeded from the previous move and decays by gravity each tick. The climbable exemption — from.isOnClimbable() clamps the allowed descent to -Magic.CLIMBABLE_MAX_SPEED and tags the move 'v_climbable' — is gated on the block cache reporting an actual ladder or vine at the player's position.

A spider climb runs against a plain wall: no climbable block sits under the player, so the exemption never applies and the constant +0.2 ascent is measured against a decaying jump allowance that falls below 0.2 within a few ticks. The violation ((max(hDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0) + max(yDistanceAboveLimit, 0.0)) * 100) then fires and handleViolation set-backs the player to the stored location. The module's onGround claims are irrelevant: NCP's ground state comes from its own block scan, not the packet flag.

countering.label: Flight17 (ascent accumulator)
countering.explanation:
Arc v2's Flight17 distinguishes ladder climbing from generic ascent. isClimbing comes from LocationHelper.isClimbing, which tests the block at the player's position for ladder or vine — so the FastLadder checks (ascend-ladder speed cap, default 0.1176, and the instant-ladder patch) stay silent for a wall climb. The generic ascent branch is what fires: validVerticalMove (no vehicle, not a step, not climbing) with isAscending and ladderTime at 2 or below triggers the ascent accumulator, which compares the vertical distance from the last ground location against ascend-distance (default 1.4) and the sustained ascent count against ascend-time (default 7).

A 0.2-per-tick climb crosses both thresholds around the seventh tick of a continuous ascent and flags 'Flight (Ascension)' — the module's climb has no vanilla counterpart to explain, because vanilla ascends only in short jump impulses. The ladder-specific caps are bypassed by design; the generic accumulator is not.

countering.label: Fly (air gravity prediction)
countering.explanation:
Hawk's Fly predicts the player's Y from an air gravity model: each tick the expected velocity is (previous - 0.08) * 0.98, and the check punishes any move whose Y lands more than DISCREPANCY_THRESHOLD (0.0001) away from the predicted position. The check is skipped entirely when the from-location is actually climbable — isInClimbable tests for ladder or vine at the block under the player (line 374) — which is the exemption genuine ladder users need.

A spider climb runs against a plain wall, so the exemption never applies and each +0.2 move lands roughly 0.2 above the predicted descending position — a discrepancy thousands of times the threshold — so punishAndTryRubberband fires on the first few moves. The file's own TODO notes that a fast-ladder check is still needed so players cannot 'pop' off real climbables; the wall-climb variant is exactly the case the exemption was never meant to cover.
